key_insight: The paper introduces a multi-block, single-probe variance reduction estimator that can track many coupled inner functions efficiently even when only O(1) blocks are sampled per iteration.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster and more sample-efficient optimization for large-scale coupled compositional learning systems, including multi-task and deep AUC maximization workloads.
method: MSVR tracks the vector of inner mappings g(w) using partial block sampling instead of probing all m blocks.
The estimator is integrated into new algorithms for finite-sum coupled compositional optimization across non-convex, convex, strongly convex, and PL settings.
The framework also improves m-dependence when outer gradients ∇f_i are linear.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved sample complexities across multiple optimization regimes and superior empirical performance on multi-task deep AUC maximization.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of partial block sampling and careful implementation of the estimator update rules to avoid bias or instability.
paper_title: Solving Finite-sum Coupled Compositional Optimization via Multi-block-Single-probe Estimator
